source: assets/ground_truth/internal_inbox/designer_reference_slides.pptx slide 21 ('Roadmap & Timeline – Phase 2.0'). The original has 4 phase blocks with rounded-corner duration tags ('6 weeks', '8 weeks', '6 weeks') and 'Feedback Alignment' descriptions per phase, connected by directional arrows. This example reproduces the 4-phase shape with simplified phase contents (number + name + 2-3 activity bullets + duration pill) and a horizontal connector line tying the discs together.
intent: Dense 4-phase rollout slide where each phase carries a number, name, set of 2-3 activities, and an explicit duration. Use for program plans that span 16-32 weeks across 4 distinct phases (Foundation → MVP → Scale → Production is the canonical shape). Distinct from development_arc (3 phases with risk callouts) — choose phase_rollout when the audience needs to see week durations and concrete activities per phase.
invariants: exactly 4 phase columns laid out horizontally
horizontal connector line behind the phase discs
each phase: numbered disc on the connector line + phase name + duration pill + activity card with 2-3 bulleted items
phase number disc uses accent_1 fill with text_on_dark (no separate rect — text shape's own fill draws the disc)
duration pill uses accent_2 fill with text_on_dark, kicker type style
activity card has bg_primary fill with subtle accent_6 outline; bullet markers are small accent_1 squares
no risk callouts (use development_arc for that pattern)
variables: phase name (1-2 words: Foundation / MVP / Scale / Production / Discovery / Pilot / Rollout / Hand-off)
phase duration ('4 weeks' / '6 weeks' / '8 weeks' / '12 weeks')
activity bullets (3 per phase, 4-7 words each, action-led verb opener)
headline (claim with total program duration mentioned)
